title: Closed immersions of algebraic spaces descend along affine inverse limits
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. A morphism $a:A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BC$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C\to B$; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact. A space is quasi-separated if its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-separated. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$. Let $U_0,V_0$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $T_{i_0}$, and let $h_0:U_0\to V_0$ be a $T_{i_0}$-morphism which is locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $U_i=U_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $V_i=V_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, and $h_i:U_i\to V_i$ for $i\ge i_0$, and $U=U_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $V=V_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $h:U\to V$ for the limit base change. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism whose every base change to a scheme is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $h$ is a closed immersion, there is $i\ge i_0$ such that $h_i$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 0850 (lemma-descend-closed-immersion), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to affine scheme bases.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement], choose an affine scheme $C_0$ and a representable surjective etale map $p_0:C_0\to V_0$. Put $C_i=C_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $C=C_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $W_i=U_i\times_{V_i}C_i$, and $W=U\times_V C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $T$ is affine. Since $C_0,T_i,T_{i_0},T$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] show that $C_i,C$ are affine schemes. The maps $p_i:C_i\to V_i$ and $p:C\to V$ are base changes of $p_0$, hence representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

Let $W_0=U_0\times_{V_0}C_0$. Affine schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] shows that $W_0$ and every $W_i=W_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $j\ge i\ge i_0$, the transition $W_j\to W_i$ is the base change of $T_j\to T_i$, so it is affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. The base-change/limit clause of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], applied to the sheaf limit of the $T_i$ and the map $W_0\to T_{i_0}$, identifies $W$ with $\varprojlim_{i\ge i_0}W_i$. The identification uses only fibre-product associativity: on a test scheme both sides are a section of $U_0$, a section of $C_0$, and a compatible family of sections of $T_i$, with the same images in $V_0$ and $T_{i_0}$. Likewise $C=\varprojlim C_i$. The index tail is small, nonempty and directed; it is cofinal since an upper bound of $i_0$ and any given index belongs to it.

The scheme test $C\to V$ of the assumed closed immersion $h$ makes $W\to C$ a closed immersion of schemes. Since $C$ is affine, the affine-quotient characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $W$ affine. Apply the eventual-affineness clause of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] to the system $(W_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ of step 2. It gives $k\ge i_0$ for which $W_k$ is an affine scheme, and the same holds at every later stage.

The map $g_k:W_k\to C_k$ is the base change of $h_0$ along $C_k\to V_0$. The arbitrary-base-change clause and the algebraic-space compatibility clause of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus] show that $g_k$ is locally of finite type as a scheme morphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] to $g_k$ over the inverse system $(T_i)_{i\ge k}$. Its stage base $T_k$ and source and target $W_k,C_k$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Its base change to $T$ is the closed immersion $W\to C$, and its base change to $T_i$ is $g_i:W_i\to C_i$: both identifications retain the same entries in the fibre products. All the scheme descent hypotheses therefore hold. We obtain $j\ge k$ for which $g_j$ is a closed immersion.

The affine schemes $W_j,C_j$ give an affine morphism $g_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Since $p_j:C_j\to V_j$ is surjective etale, [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] implies that $h_j$ is affine and in particular representable. Apply [lem-trf-space-closed-immersion-cover-descent] with $E=U_j$, $B=Y=V_j$, $b=\mathrm{id}$ and the singleton cover $p_j$. Its pulled-back morphism is $g_j$, a closed immersion; every further scheme test is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Thus $h_j$ is a closed immersion, as required. This application uses representability already proved here, rather than assuming it from the limit.

The statement is byte-identical to live and matches Stacks 0850 in Situation 084W (spaces-limits.tex l.1449, l.1670-1691), with affine scheme bases: qcqs U_0 and V_0, h_0 locally of finite type, nonempty directed index, no added hypothesis. There are no new nodes; the item is unsplit on live and side-live, there is no repair note and no SGA. The 5 steps follow the Stacks proof and I checked each against the cited statements. (1) An affine atlas C_0 (03H6 node); C_i and C are affine by 01SH plus permanence (1),(2); p_i is a base change of p_0, so surjective etale (02X2 node). (2) W_0 and W_i are qcqs by the product clause; transition maps are affine by space affine base change; W = lim W_i by the last clause of the affine-limits node; the scheme limit T equals the sheaf limit by Yoneda. (3) W -> C is a closed immersion of schemes, so W is affine by the 01QO clause; the eventual-affine clause gives an affine W_k. (4) g_k is locally of finite type by the finite-type calculus node (base change plus agreement for spaces); 01ZP applies to the qcqs affine T_k, W_k, C_k, and its base changes are the W_i and W. (5) g_j is affine (01SH), so h_j is affine and hence representable by affine-locality; 03KD cover descent with B=Y=V_j, b=id and the single map p_j, together with 01QR, gives that h_j is a closed immersion. This last step replaces Stacks' integral-local citation and is valid. Q115's qcqs-base-descend-closed-immersion assumes finite presentation, so it is not a duplicate. I accept tool_uses 03H6, 02X2, 01YX, 01ZP and 03KD. All four are accepted. Edge cases checked: empty spaces (Spec 0 atlas), a constant system, non-Noetherian bases.
